fullPassage: To illustrate the benefits of simplifying the observer's job, consider psychologist William Ickes's research on "everyday mind reading." One way he studies such mind reading is by having two strangers interact. He tapes the interaction and then has each participant view the tape. Participants are to stop the tape at different points and say what they are thinking. Then, participants see the tape again and are to stop it at different points and write down what their interaction partner was thinking at that point. Observers rate the degree to which the participant's guess about what the partner was thinking matches what the partner was actually thinking. Ickes could have had observers make their judgments on a 0 (not at all) to 100 (completely) scale. However, he had observers use a 3-point scale with "0" being "essentially different content," "1" being "similar, but not the same, content," and "2" being "essentially the same content." By using fewer categories, raters found the job of rating easier and were able to make reliable ratings.

However, he had observers use a 3-point scale with "0" being "essentially different content," "1" being "similar, but not the same, content," and "2" being "essentially the same content." By using fewer categories, raters found the job of rating easier and were able to make reliable ratings.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ have → has: 주어 He(William Ickes)가 3인칭 단수이므로 동사 has가 와야 한다. ← 정답
det.analysis:
✅ ① simplifying: 전치사 of의 목적어로 동명사 simplifying이 쓰인 올바른 어법
✅ ② is: 'One way he studies such mind reading is by having ~'에서 주어 One way가 단수이므로 is는 올바른 어법
❌ ③ have → has: 'He tapes the interaction and then have each participant view the tape'에서 주어 He가 3인칭 단수이므로 has가 와야 함. have는 수 일치 위반 ← 정답
✅ ④ what: 'write down what their interaction partner was thinking'에서 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사 what이 올바른 어법

det.korean: ④ unreliable → reliable: 본문은 적은 범주를 사용함으로써 신뢰성 있는 평가를 할 수 있었다는 긍정적 결론을 제시한다. ← 정답
det.analysis:
✅ ① benefits: '관찰자의 작업을 단순화하는 이점'이라는 문맥에 적절
✅ ② interact: '두 명의 낯선 사람이 상호작용하게 하는' 실험 방법에 적절
✅ ③ rate: '관찰자가 일치 정도를 평가한다'는 실험 절차에 적절
❌ ④ unreliable → reliable: 본문 결론은 '적은 범주 → 신뢰성 있는 평가'라는 긍정적 효과. unreliable은 논지와 정반대 ← 정답
det.tip: 본문의 핵심 논지는 '단순화의 이점'. 마지막 문장의 결론이 긍정적이어야 합니다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② complicating → simplifying: 본문 첫 문장은 '단순화하는' 이점을 설명하며, 본문 전체가 단순화의 효과를 보여준다. ← 정답

✅ ① strangers: '두 명의 낯선 사람이 상호작용하게 한다'는 실험 설계에 적절
❌ ② complicating → simplifying: 'the benefits of complicating'이 되면 결론의 '적은 범주 → 쉽고 신뢰성 있는 평가'와 모순 ← 정답
✅ ③ fewer: '더 적은 범주를 사용함으로써'라는 단순화 핵심 방법에 적절

det.korean: 적은 범주를 사용함으로써 평가자들은 __________ 작업을 더 쉽게 할 수 있었다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① thinking(생각하기): 참가자의 활동이지 평가자의 작업이 아님
❌ ② interact(상호작용하기): 낯선 사람들의 활동이지 평가자의 작업이 아님

✅ ④ rating(평가하기): 'raters found the job of ____ easier'에서 평가자(raters)의 핵심 작업은 rating ← 정답
det.tip: raters의 작업(job)이 무엇인지 본문 전체의 실험 설계에서 파악하세요.

det.korean: 적은 범주를 사용함으로써 평가자들은 평가 작업을 더 쉽게 할 수 있었고 __________ 평가를 할 수 있었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① reliable(신뢰할 수 있는): 단순화 → 쉬움 + 신뢰성이 핵심 논지 ← 정답
❌ ② different(다른): 3점 척도에서 '0'의 의미에 쓰인 단어이나 평가의 질을 수식하기 부적절
❌ ③ similar(유사한): 3점 척도에서 '1'의 의미에 쓰인 단어이나 평가의 신뢰도를 나타내지 않음
❌ ④ easier(더 쉬운): 앞에서 이미 사용된 표현. and 이후 같은 의미 반복은 부자연스러움
det.tip: and로 연결된 두 절은 서로 다른 결과를 제시합니다. easier(쉬움) + ?(신뢰도).

questions.passage: To illustrate the benefits of simplifying the observer's job, consider psychologist William Ickes's research on "<u>everyday mind reading</u>." One way he studies such mind reading is by having two strangers interact. He tapes the interaction and then has each participant view the tape. Participants are to stop the tape at different points and say what they are thinking. Then, participants see the tape again and are to stop it at different points and write down what their interaction partner was thinking at that point. Observers rate the degree to which the participant's guess about what the partner was thinking matches what the partner was actually thinking. Ickes could have had observers make their judgments on a 0 (not at all) to 100 (completely) scale. However, he had observers use a 3-point scale with "0" being "essentially different content," "1" being "similar, but not the same, content," and "2" being "essentially the same content." By using fewer categories, raters found the job of rating easier and were able to make reliable ratings.
